title: The One on the Left
hook: No sign. The car on your left waits.
scene: Overcast morning, a downtown cross with no sign and no light — two two-lanes meeting like someone forgot the post. You and a gray primer car arrive together. They are on your left. You are on their right. Their nose is already creeping. Yours wants to match it. The Core still has corners that never got a face.
decision: You arrive together and they are on your left. Who goes?

options.text: You go — they are on your left, so they wait
options.result: You take the crossing at a crawl. They hold. Two cars, one rule, no horn. The corner that never got a sign still had an order.

options.text: Wave them through so you do not have to own the corner
options.result: You wave. They wave. Nobody goes, then both go. Noses meet in the middle. Politeness invented a tie the paint already broke.

options.text: Stop long enough that they get tired and go, then follow
options.result: You plant it like a sign that is not there. They finally go, late. The car behind you does not know why you died at an empty corner. You taught the block to stall.

options.text: Go together and split the middle — you arrived as a pair
options.result: You both take it. The middle is one plow wide. Steel on a primer quarter. Arriving together is why one of you waits, not why both of you go.

debrief: At a crossing with no sign and no light, yield to the driver on your right. If they are on your left, you go. Do not wave the order away.

source.psdp_skill: Skill ten: city driving – part two
source.teaching_target: At an uncontrolled intersection, the vehicle on the left yields to the vehicle on the right.
